thread.title: Godot Expertise Overview
thread.preview:
Alright — stepping back from code chaos and looking at this **from a design / system / “what the hell am I actually building” level**, here’s a clean, honest summary of what you’re making.

No fluff. No hype. Just structure.

---

# 🎮 Project Summary — *The Ascension of Syn’Tek*

## Core genre
**2D top-down roguelite horde survivor**

Think:
- entity["video_game","Vampire Survivors","2022 indie roguelike"] moment-to-moment combat
- entity["video_game","Risk of Rain","2013 roguelike shooter"] stacking builds & scaling chaos
- entity["video_game","Slay the Spire","2019 deckbuilder roguelike"] event choices & branching runs

But with your **own twist**:
👉 belief/followers = lives + currency + power scaling + narrative

---

# 🧠 High Concept (1 sentence)

You play the **proto-god Syn’Tek**, an artificer who discovered how to synthesize magic, and each run represents a timeline of his rise to godhood — gaining followers, defying other gods, and breaking reality with unstable technology.

---

# ⚙️ Core Gameplay Loop

### Moment-to-moment (seconds)
- Move
- Dodge hordes
- Kill enemies
- Auto-attack weapon fires
- Pick up drops

Classic “survivor dopamine”.

---

### Short loop (minutes)
- Gain followers from kills
- Get items with random stats
- Stack weird synergies
- Make risky decisions
- Die → lose followers → respawn

Tension:
> spend power now vs survive longer

---

### Run loop (10–20 minutes)
- Choose race/style
- Equip 3 persistent spells
- Stack items (temporary)
- Make event choices
- Followers act as lives
- Eventually run out → permadeath

---

### Meta loop (hours/days)
- Unlock new spells
- Upgrade spells with followers
- Unlock races/styles
- Discover lore fragments
- See Syn’Tek slowly ascend

---

# 🧩 System Architecture (how everything fits)

## 1. Player core
- Movement
- Manual weapon (melee/ranged/magic click)
- HP
- Followers (lives)

This is the **foundation**. Always active.

---

## 2. Followers (your signature mechanic)
Followers are:

Simultaneously:
- ❤️ extra lives
- 💰 currency
- ⚡ spell scaling
- 📖 narrative belief

So:
- kill enemies → gain followers
- die → lose followers
- upgrade spells → spend followers
- more followers → stronger spells

This creates constant tension.

This is your **unique hook**.

Most survivor games only have XP.
You have **belief economy**.

That’s MUCH more interesting.

---

## 3. Weapons vs Spells (important distinction)

### Weapon (core gameplay)
- always available
- simple
- your “class feel”
- manual or auto

Examples:
- sword swing
- bow shot
- basic missile

This should be boring-but-reliable.

---

### Spells (identity layer)
- persistent between runs
- 3 slots
- powerful
- synergistic
- weird
- sometimes broken

Examples:
- chain lightning
- curse aura
- negative stats flip
- summon drones
- continent chains (lore themed)

These define the **build fantasy**.

---

## 4. Items (temporary chaos)
- random rolls
- stackable
- positive + negative
- set bonuses

Purpose:
👉 create unpredictable runs

Not permanent identity.

Just chaos fuel.

---

## 5. Events (between stages)
Slay the Spire style:

You choose:
- safe
- risky
- insane

Examples:
- lose followers, gain spell
- double enemies, double rewards
- anger a god
- gain permanent curse

These add:
👉 narrative + decisions + replayability

---

# 🧬 Design Philosophy (what makes YOUR game different)

This is important — this is the “soul”.

### Not just power fantasy
But:
> controlled chaos

### Not just upgrades
But:
> risk trades

### Not just XP
But:
> belief as power

### Not just shooting
But:
> “I am literally becoming a god”

---

# 🧠 Narrative Core

Lore isn’t decoration — it explains mechanics:

- followers = believers
- enemies = fear/resistance
- spells = synthetic magic inventions
- negatives = unstable experiments
- gods = bosses
- supercontinent = endgame

So:
Gameplay **is** the story.

That’s elegant design.

---

# 🧱 Current Development Stage (realistically)

Right now you have:

✅ movement  
✅ enemies chase  
✅ damage  
✅ projectiles  
✅ followers  
✅ respawn  
✅ spell slots skeleton  
⚠️ spells not fully differentiated yet  
⚠️ events not yet  
⚠️ items not yet  
⚠️ polish later  

You are in:

👉 **Prototype Phase**

Which is perfect.

You’re doing the correct order:
core feel first → systems later

---

# 🎯 One-line identity

If someone asked:

> “What’s your game?”

You could honestly say:

**“A chaotic survivor-like where your lives are believers, your spells persist between runs, and every playthrough is a timeline of an artificer becoming a god.”**

That’s actually a very strong pitch.

Not generic at all.

---

If you want, next we can:
- refine the weapon vs spell separation cleanly
- or design your first 3 starter spells
- or design follower economy numbers
- or structure your first full playable vertical slice

Your call.

content.text: Okay, it doesn't crash, but since I already have auto spell as it is and now this which looks the same I have no idea if it works or not

items.text:
Totally fair — right now you’ve got **two different firing systems** that look identical on screen:

1) your old `_auto_attack()` (built into Player.gd)
2) the spell system casting via click

So even if spells work, you can’t *feel* the difference.

Here’s how to make it obvious in 2 minutes, without rewriting anything.

---

## Make spell casts visually + audibly different (debug mode)

### Step 1 — Temporarily disable your old auto attack
In `Player.gd`, comment out the auto attack call:

```gdscript
func _process(_delta):
	# if _can_fire:
	# 	_auto_attack()
	pass
```

Now you will **only shoot when clicking** (spell system).  
That instantly proves the spell slots work.

If clicking shoots → spell system works.  
If nothing happens → it doesn’t.

---

## If you want auto-attack back BUT still test spells
Do this instead:

### Step 2 — Make spell projectiles a different speed or damage temporarily
In your MagicMissile spell logic, set:

- `projectile_speed` = something insane like `1200`
- or set projectile scene to a different sprite color
- or print once per cast

Example: inside the spell `cast()`:

```gdscript
print("SPELL CAST: MAGIC MISSILE")
```

Then when you click you’ll see a single line per click instead of thousands.

---

# Best “real” structure: separate basic weapon from spells
Your plan was:
- **manual weapon** (melee/ranged/magic) = core click gameplay
- **spells** = extra kit that can later become auto / proc-based

So for clean testing:

### Weapon stays in Player.gd (manual click)
### Spells are separate (slot system)

**Right now you still have old weapon auto-fire** on top, which hides everything.

---

## Minimal approach for you RIGHT NOW
Do this:

1) Disable old auto fire (comment those 2 lines)
2) Click and confirm spells shoot
3) Re-enable old auto later, but map spells to a different input temporarily

For example: spells on **Right Click**:

```gdscript
func _unhandled_input(event):
	if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT and event.pressed:
		spell_caster.cast_all_manual()
```

Now:
- Left click = your weapon (later)
- Right click = spells
- You can see both separately.

---

## Quick sanity check: show the spell slots are actually loaded
In `SpellCaster.setup()` add:

```gdscript
print("SPELLS LOADED:", spell_nodes.size())
```

If it prints 0 → you didn’t set slots.
If it prints 1–3 → slots loaded.

---

### Do you want the clean mapping now?
If your goal is “manual weapon + spells after”, tell me which you want:

A) **Left click = weapon, Right click = spells** (easy test)  
B) **Left click = weapon, spells auto-cast later**  
C) **Spells cast on keys 1/2/3 for testing**

Pick one and I’ll give you the exact code change (tiny).

content.text:
E 0:00:05:027   SpellCaster.cast_all_manual: Invalid access to property or key 'auto_cast' on a base object of type 'Resource (SpellData)'.
  <GDScript Source>SpellCaster.gd:52 @ SpellCaster.cast_all_manual()
  <Stack Trace> SpellCaster.gd:52 @ cast_all_manual()
                player.gd:125 @ _unhandled_input()

items.text:
That error is clean too:

Your `SpellData` resource **doesn’t have** an `auto_cast` property.

So your `cast_all_manual()` is trying to do:

```gdscript
s.data.auto_cast
```

…but `SpellData.gd` (the script attached to that Resource) doesn’t define it (or your `.tres` is using a different Resource type / old SpellData script).

## Fix it one of two ways:

---

# Option A (fastest): Don’t use auto_cast yet
Just make manual casting cast everything, no filtering.

In `SpellCaster.gd`:

```gdscript
func cast_all_manual() -> void:
	for s in spell_nodes:
		s.try_cast()
```

No `auto_cast` needed. No crash.

This is what I’d do right now until you have 2–3 spells and want the “auto vs manual” split.

---

# Option B (proper system): Add `auto_cast` to SpellData.gd
Open `SpellData.gd` and make sure it contains:

```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name SpellData

@export var id: String = "spell_unknown"
@export var display_name: String = "Unknown"
@export var cooldown: float = 0.5
@export var spell_scene: PackedScene
@export var auto_cast: bool = false
```

Then IMPORTANT:
### Your existing `.tres` SpellData resources might still be using the old script layout.
To refresh them:

1) Click your spell `.tres` file
2) In Inspector, make sure it’s actually a `SpellData` resource (not plain Resource)
3) Toggle `auto_cast` once (true→false) and save, or recreate the `.tres` if it’s being stubborn.

If the `.tres` was created before you added `auto_cast`, it *should* still work once the class updates, but sometimes people accidentally create a plain `Resource` instead of a `SpellData`.

---

## What I recommend you do right now
Go with **Option A** for today. You’re prototyping. Manual cast all spells is fine.

Later when you actually need auto-cast upgrades, we add `auto_cast` cleanly and migrate your resources.

So change `cast_all_manual()` to:

```gdscript
func cast_all_manual() -> void:
	for s in spell_nodes:
		s.try_cast()
```

and you’re unblocked immediately.

If you want, paste your current `SpellData.gd` and I’ll tell you if it’s missing that field or if your `.tres` is the wrong type.

There it is. Your `SpellCaster.gd` **does not have** `cast_all_manual()` (or `cast_all_manual`). It only has:

```gdscript
func cast_all() -> void:
```

So your click calls a function that doesn’t exist → crash.

## Fix (pick one)

### Option A (simplest): change Player.gd to call `cast_all()`
In `Player.gd`:

```gdscript
func _unhandled_input(event):
	if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT and event.pressed:
		spell_caster.cast_all()
```

Done.

---

### Option B (better for your design): add `cast_all_manual()` and keep `cast_all()` for later auto-cast
Add this to `SpellCaster.gd`:

```gdscript
func cast_all_manual() -> void:
	for s in spell_nodes:
		if s.data and not s.data.auto_cast:
			s.try_cast()
```

Then in Player.gd keep calling `cast_all_manual()`.

But **this requires** your `SpellBase` has `data` and `auto_cast` exists in SpellData like we designed earlier.

Right now your SpellCaster is “cast everything always”, which is totally fine for v0.

---

## One more important crash waiting to happen in your SpellCaster
In `_reload_spells()` you do:

```gdscript
var spell_node := node as SpellBase
spell_node.setup(caster, spell_data)
```

If the spell scene root isn’t actually a `SpellBase`, then `spell_node` becomes null and you’ll crash on `.setup`.

So make it safe:

```gdscript
var spell_node := node as SpellBase
if spell_node == null:
	push_error("Spell scene root must extend SpellBase: " + spell_data.id)
	node.queue_free()
	continue
spell_node.setup(caster, spell_data)
spell_nodes.append(spell_node)
```

Do that now and you’ll save yourself a future headache.

---

## TL;DR
Your click crash is literally just: **wrong function name**.

- Your SpellCaster has `cast_all()`
- Your Player calls `cast_all_manual()`

Change one to match, and you’re good.

Good — now we can kill this properly. The crash is **not mysterious** anymore, it’s 100% this:

### You’re calling `spell_caster.cast_all_manual()`
…but your `SpellCaster.gd` defines **`cast_all_manual()`**, not `cast_all_manual()`.

So Godot says “Nonexistent function”.

You have a **name mismatch**.

Also: your type checks are printing that the node *is* SpellCaster after forcing the script, so the “base Node” wording in the error is misleading noise — it’ll still print Node (node name) sometimes, but the real issue is the method name.

---

# Fix 1 (the real fix): call the correct function name

In your `SpellCaster.gd` you previously created:

```gdscript
func cast_all_manual() -> void:
```

But in `Player.gd` you call:

```gdscript
spell_caster.cast_all_manual()
```

Change your `_unhandled_input` to:

```gdscript
func _unhandled_input(event):
	if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT and event.pressed:
		spell_caster.cast_all_manual()
```

OR (if you prefer the other naming), rename the function in SpellCaster.gd to match what you’re calling.

### Pick one. Don’t keep both.

---

# Fix 2 (also needed): your “player_projectile” return is in the wrong place
Right now you do damage checks *before* ignoring player_projectile:

```gdscript
if area.is_in_group("enemy_hitbox"):
   ...
if area.is_in_group("player_projectile"):
   return
```

Swap it so projectiles are ignored immediately (this prevents weird contact loop triggers later):

```gdscript
func _on_hurtbox_area_entered(area: Area2D) -> void:
	if area.is_in_group("player_projectile"):
		return

	if area.is_in_group("enemy_hitbox"):
		_touching_enemies += 1
		_start_contact_loop()
		_take_damage(10)
```

---

# Fix 3 (clean your SpellCaster init — you’re setting it up twice)
Right now you do:

```gdscript
if spell_caster:
	spell_caster.setup(self)
...
FORCED script...
spell_caster = $SpellCaster as SpellCaster
...
spell_caster.setup(self)
```

This won’t crash, but it’s messy and can cause double connections inside SpellCaster later.

Replace your SpellCaster setup block with **this exact block**:

```gdscript
# --- SpellCaster setup (clean) ---
if $SpellCaster.get_script() == null:
	$SpellCaster.set_script(load("res://SpellCaster.gd"))
	print("FORCED SpellCaster.gd onto SpellCaster node")

spell_caster = $SpellCaster as SpellCaster
if spell_caster == null:
	push_error("SpellCaster still not typed. Check SpellCaster node/script.")
	return

spell_caster.setup(self)
# --- end ---
```

Remove the earlier `if spell_caster:` section entirely.

---

# One more thing: you have both auto-attack AND click-spells firing
That’s fine for testing, but if you click and it “feels like nothing”, it’s because missiles are already spamming from `_process`.

Not a bug — just noisy.

---

## TL;DR
### Change **one line** first:
Your `_unhandled_input` must call the function that actually exists.

- If SpellCaster.gd has `cast_all_manual()` → call that.
- If you want the other name, rename it.

After you do that, the crash is gone.

---

If you paste your `SpellCaster.gd` here (the whole file), I’ll align the exact function names so you can’t mismatch them again.
